title: Find The First Player to win K Games in a Row
summary: In a competition with n players, each having a unique skill level, players are queued from 0 to n-1.
statement: In a competition with n players, each having a unique skill level, players are queued from 0 to n-1. Players take turns playing games, with the higher-skilled player winning. The winner remains at the front, and the loser goes to the end of the queue. The first player to win k consecutive games is declared the winner. Return the starting position of this player.
constraints: skills contains at least two distinct skill values and k is positive.
The first two queued players compete; the stronger remains first and the loser moves to the back.
Return the original zero-based index of the first player to win k consecutive games.
reference_solution:
def first_consecutive_game_winner(skills,k):
    champion=0;streak=0
    for challenger in range(1,len(skills)):
        if skills[champion]>skills[challenger]:streak+=1
        else:champion=challenger;streak=1
        if streak>=k:return champion
    return champion

hints: Once a player loses, they cannot matter before the current champion faces every later player; the global maximum never loses.
Scan challengers in original order while tracking the front champion and its current consecutive wins.
Champion win increments streak; challenger win replaces champion with streak one; return on k or final champion.
This scan matches the actual sequence until the maximum reaches the front, after which it wins forever, so no explicit queue rotation is needed.

tests.explanation: Player zero wins once, then original player two defeats players zero and three consecutively and wins.
The maximum-skill player at index one eventually stays in front forever and reaches any large streak.
